title: Capital Credits Accounting Note — Present Value of a Distribution-Margin Row Retired Early at a Discount
content:
# Present Value of a Distribution-Margin Row Retired Early at a Discount

*Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) — accounting note on the payable of a discounted early retirement.*

## Valuation clause

The payable of a distribution-margin row retired under an approved discounted early retirement is its gross, the allocated amount of that allocation year and source still unretired, discounted at the patron class's early retirement discount rate a year, compounded once a year, over the whole number of years from the calendar year of the retirement to the year the row would be retired in the general rotation, its allocation year plus the class's expected rotation years, never fewer than zero years; the payable is rounded half up to the cent. A payable is never below zero.

## Terms of the clause

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Request | the member's discounted early retirement request on the account in board-approved status, the most recently submitted one where there are several |
| Row | one distribution-margin allocation year of the account, valued on its own |
| Gross | the allocated amount of that year and source less every general retirement already booked on it |
| Year of the retirement | the calendar year in which the row is booked |
| Rotation year | the row's allocation year plus the class's expected rotation years |
| Years of discount | the whole years from the year of the retirement to the rotation year; zero where the rotation year is the year of the retirement or earlier |
| Rate | the class's early retirement discount rate, a percent a year |

**How the discount is applied.** One plus the rate, written as a decimal, is raised to the power of the years of discount; the gross divided by that amount is the payable, rounded half up to the cent at the end and not before.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

The rate of 6 percent and the expected rotation of 20 years below are assumed for this illustration only.

**Row A.** A 2012 distribution-margin allocation of $640.00 with nothing yet retired is retired in calendar year 2026.

1. Gross: $640.00.
2. Rotation year: 2012 plus 20, that is 2032.
3. Years of discount: from 2026 to 2032, 6 whole years.
4. One plus the rate (1.06) raised to the power 6 is 1.418519.
5. $640.00 divided by 1.418519 is $451.17.

**Row B.** A 2005 distribution-margin allocation with $210.00 still unretired, retired in 2026. Its rotation year is 2025, earlier than 2026, so the years of discount are zero and the payable is the full $210.00.

## Points of judgement

- Each allocation year is valued separately; rows are never totalled before discounting or before rounding.
- The years of discount are whole calendar years counted between the two years; no part year is counted.
- The rounding is half up and happens once, on the payable of the row.
